newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt asks confidence vote on budget measures.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt asks confidence vote on budget measures.

text.p: The Italian government on Monday asked for a confidence vote in the lower house of parliament over measures introduced at the end of 1996 which are designed to raise around 4.3 trillion lire ($2.59 billion).

The package, tied to the 1997 budget, still has to be approved by parliament but has been weighed down by hundreds of opposition amendments. If a government loses a confidence vote it automatically has to resign.
A parliamentary official said Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco had formally requested the vote to sidestep the amendments and push the package into law.
Parliamentary party leaders were due to decide later on Monday when the vote would be held. State television said it would probably take place on Tuesday.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left coalition relies on the hardleft Communist Refoundation for its majority in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house). Refoundation has previously given its backing to the year-end budget measures.

The government called several confidence motions in both the upper and lower house of parliament last year to sweep aside opposition filibustering on a wide range of legislation, winning all the votes with ease.
